svg.title: How counselling is paid for in British Columbia
svg.desc: Three bands describing the routes to paying for counselling in BC: extended health benefits, public and no-cost services, and paying privately.
svg.text: The three routes to paying for counselling in BC

text.tspan: An employer or student plan with a per-year counselling maximum. Whether a Registered Clinical Counsellor is eligible is
plan-specific — confirm the designation with your insurer, not just the dollar amount.
Health-authority mental health teams, community agencies, campus counselling, employee and family assistance programs, and
crisis lines. Free or low cost, usually with waitlists or session caps.
Paying the session fee directly. No referral, no waitlist, no session cap, and no diagnosis on a file. The trade-off is cost —
which is why the free consultation exists before you commit to anything.
MSP does not cover counselling delivered in private practice by a Registered Clinical Counsellor.
